groups.title: RESTful API Design in Laravel
groups.question: A mobile team uses your Laravel API, and renaming a database column broke their app. Explain how API resources and versioning protect clients.

followUps.API Resources and Transforming Eloquent: What do API Resources do between your models and the JSON response?
followUps.API Versioning Strategy: How would you version the API so old app versions keep working?

evidence.text: API Resources turn models into the JSON shape clients receive.
They separate the database structure from the public API.
Renaming a column only requires updating the resource, not every client.
Versions are separated with URL prefixes like /api/v1 or with headers.
A new version can change the contract while the old one keeps working.
Old versions are retired only after clients have moved.

notEnough: Only saying you add a version number.

groups.title: JSON Response Patterns
groups.question: Different endpoints return errors in different shapes and some return 200 with an error message. Explain how you would make responses consistent and meaningful.

followUps.Consistent Error Response Structure: How would you give every API error the same shape?
followUps.HTTP Status Codes and Semantic Responses: Which status codes would you use for create, delete, invalid input and not found?

evidence.text: Laravel's exception handler can turn all API errors into one JSON format.
The format includes a message and, for validation, field errors.
Clients can then handle every error the same way.

notEnough: Only saying you return JSON errors.

evidence.text: 201 for created and 204 for a delete with no body.
422 for invalid input and 404 when the resource does not exist.
Correct codes let clients, caches and monitoring react properly.

groups.title: Laravel Sanctum API Tokens
groups.question: A reporting integration should only read orders, and a leaked token must be stoppable immediately. Explain how Sanctum tokens handle permissions and revocation.

followUps.Token Abilities and Scoped Permissions: How do token abilities limit what a token can do?
followUps.Token Expiration and Revocation: How do you revoke a token or make tokens expire?

evidence.text: Tokens are created with ability strings like read:orders.
Code checks tokenCan before allowing an action.
Giving each token only the abilities it needs limits damage if it leaks.
Sanctum stores tokens in a database table.
Deleting the token record revokes it immediately.
An expiration setting makes old tokens stop working automatically.

groups.title: Rate Limiting
groups.question: Your login endpoint is being brute-forced and a partner's integration needs a higher limit than anonymous users. Explain Laravel's rate limiting.

followUps.Laravel's Built-in Rate Limiter: How do you add rate limits to routes in Laravel?
followUps.Custom Rate Limit Keys: How would you give logged-in partners a higher limit than anonymous users?

evidence.text: Named limits are defined with the RateLimiter.
The throttle middleware applies them to routes.
Strict limits on login and other auth routes slow down brute-force attacks.
Limits are keyed by something like user id or IP address.
Different limits can apply to authenticated and anonymous requests.
This keeps limits strict for unknown callers without blocking trusted ones.

notEnough: Only saying you change the limit.
